title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The handwriting is on the verso of a typescript sheet of SGA 7 exposé IX (Néron models, semi-stable reduction criterion). It is unrelated to the typed text, and probably also to the divided-power de Rham theme of the folder, except through formal schemes.

Setting: k is a field. C, C', S are (presumably cocommutative) k-coalgebras. V(C) is the associated 'variety', meaning the formal scheme or functor represented by C in the Dieudonné/Demazure–Gabriel style. In that dictionary the product V(C)×V(C') = V(C⊗C'), so the tensor product is the categorical product of cocommutative coalgebras. There are coalgebra maps C→S and C'→S. The goal is to construct the fibre product V(C)×_{V(S)}V(C'), written V(C)⊠_{V(S)}V(C') and C⊠_S C'.

Step 1 (first attempt). Take the two maps α, β: C⊗C' ⇉ C⊗C'⊗S, given by coacting with S through the C factor and through the C' factor. Set P = Ker(α−β), which is the cotensor-type equalizer.
- Since ⊗S is exact over a field, P⊗S = Ker(C⊗C'⊗S ⇉ C⊗S⊗C'⊗S).
- He asks whether α∘i = β∘i equals (i⊗id_S)∘Δ_P, i.e. whether P inherits a coaction or coalgebra structure.
- He tests this on elements: x ∈ C⊗C' with α(x)=β(x), looking at Im(x⊗S → C⊗C'⊗S).
- The answer is not automatic: P need not be a subcoalgebra.

Step 2 (fix). Iterate to get a descending chain …P_3 ⊂ P_2 ⊂ P_1 ⊂ C⊗C'. Each step imposes the equalizing condition again on the image of the comultiplication. Set P_∞ = ∩P_i.
- He notes ∩(P_i⊗S) = P_∞⊗S. This holds over a field, since tensoring with a free module commutes with intersections of subspaces.
- P_∞ is the largest subcoalgebra of C⊗C' on which the two composites to S agree, i.e. the equalizer in the category of coalgebras.

Step 3 (universal property). Any coalgebra C'' with a coalgebra map C''→C⊗C' equalizing the two maps lands in P_∞. Hence C'' → C⊠_S C' is a coalgebra homomorphism (the last line, 'hom de coalgèbres').

Marginal dual remarks:
- x⊗1−1⊗x and x⊗y−1⊗xy: generators of the ideal defining a tensor product of algebras over a subalgebra, the dual picture of the fibre product.
- u_C⊗id_{C'} = id_C⊗u_C: a compatibility of the maps to S.
- 'S^h ⊗ S^h = S', with u⊗1−1⊗u ≠ (0?).
- The phrase 'coproduit dans …' (coproduct in some category).

Overall: a routine verification that the category of (cocommutative) coalgebras over a field, i.e. formal varieties, has fibre products. They are built as largest subcoalgebras via an iterated kernel.
errors: Step 1 (P = Ker(α−β) as the fibre product) is wrong in general because P need not be a subcoalgebra. Grothendieck himself flags this with the '?' and corrects it via the descending chain P_i.
Whether the chain stabilizes is not addressed. Taking the intersection P_∞ avoids the issue, and the needed fact ∩(P_i⊗S) = (∩P_i)⊗S is correct over a field.
A shorter route exists: take the sum of all subcoalgebras contained in Ker. Not an error, just a remark.

ideas.what: Fibre product / equalizer in the category of (cocommutative) coalgebras, constructed as the largest subcoalgebra of C⊗C' on which the two maps to S agree, via an iterated descending intersection
ideas.modern_name: Limits (equalizers, pullbacks) in the category of coalgebras; cotensor product C□_S C' and its maximal subcoalgebra
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore. Cotensor products: Milnor–Moore and Eilenberg–Moore (1960s). Completeness of the coalgebra category: Barr (1974); explicit constructions: Porst, Agore (2000s).
ideas.where_published: Analogous material on formal schemes and coalgebras is in Demazure–Gabriel (1970) and Dieudonné's work on formal groups; not known in Grothendieck's own texts

ideas.what: Dictionary between coalgebras and formal 'varieties' V(C), under which ⊗ becomes the product and fibre products become ⊠_S
ideas.modern_name: Formal schemes as cocommutative coalgebras (Cartier–Dieudonné duality)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a scratch verification of a standard categorical fact (fibre products of coalgebras and formal varieties via the largest subcoalgebra). It is well known, though explicit published constructions came somewhat later (Barr, Porst, Agore). Nothing new.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: the first term reads V(P) ← V(C⊗C'), with the ⊗ written over a crossed-out symbol.
'[-x-] ∈ S' is more likely a struck-out '⊗S' / '⊗ ∈ S' fragment.
'P_∞ [-⊗S-] → C⊗C'⊗S' reads in the image as 'P_∞ ⊗S → C⊗C'⊗e' (likely a slip for S).
The bottom heading reads roughly 'coproduit dans [?] ...' with the last words illegible ('coproduit dans les … [?]').
The line 'V(C)×V(C'') → V(C'')' is followed below by 'V(S) → …'.
'S^h ⊗_h S^h = S' may be 'S^h ⊗_{S^h} S^h' or similar; uncertain.
